newsitem.title: FRANCE: French right should offer new growth plan - Giscard.
newsitem.headline: French right should offer new growth plan - Giscard.

text.p: Former Conservative President Valery Giscard d'Estaing advised France's ailing centre-right government on Wednesday to promise voters an economic growth package which would be delivered in July to tackle unemployment.

He said the ruling RPR/UFD coalition should offer a package which would be introduced a month after the parliamentary runoff and include fiscal and social measures aimed at creating three percent growth by the end of the year.

President Jacques Chirac understood that voters who swung left in last Sunday's election first round wanted a change in style but they also wanted to see change in their economic and social situation, he told France 2 television.
"I suggest that the next government set a rendezvous with growth for the first of July," he said.

They should present the National Assembly with a plan which will of course encompass what has already been done, but also fill it out with fiscal and social steps to support growth and set a goal of three percent growth by the end of the year, in other words an economic upturn which will create jobs," he said.
"The message must be put to the French people in simple terms," he said, a "pact with growth."
The government should tell the French people "if you make a mistake it could cost you dearly," he added.
Voters put the French left in the lead in the first round of the parliamentary election on Sunday, opening up the possibility of a left-wing victory after the runoff next Sunday.
